newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse pauses for breath, BUX declines.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse pauses for breath, BUX declines.

text.p: The Hungarian share market paused for breath on Thursday after setting three consecutive closing highs, traders and analysts said.
The BUX index finished at 8,433.66 points, down 50.13 points or 0.59 percent. In early trading, however, it ran up to a new trading peak of 8,627.95 points.
"On long-term the BUX index can exceed the Dow Jones but on the short-term this seems to be a wild idea," a trader said. "I think we have already exceeded a psychological level."
The Budapest Stock Exchange is the most correlated to movements on the U.S. market due to the high proportion of foreign investors in Hungary.
Andrea Dicso of Bank Austria Investment Rt said that on the short-term, the market was likely to behave as it did on Thursday.
"For Friday we expect a day of similar sentiment, with (prices) moving down or stagnating," Dicso said. "What we have now is a healthy correction after recent days' rises."

Dicso said she expected the next week to remain positive. "If anytime, falls could be expected after the release of first half earnings." Hungarian companies have to submit their results by August 15.
Another analyst said Thursday's fall was just profit-taking and not a real correction. But she also expected the market's positive sentiment to prevail next week.
"I think until the earnings reports of OTP Bank and MOL the market would move upwards," said Gabriella Bor of New York Broker Budapest. "But after that the market may give up five to ten percent."
On Thursday, recent heavy gainers, including MOL which fell 85 forints to 5,130, closed lower.

MOL, downgraded by CS First Boston to 'hold' from 'buy', said it signed a five billion forints credit line agreement with a bank consortium for five years, and also signed a 20-year agreement with Csepel Power Plant Rt, wholly owned by PowerGen, to supply natural gas for a power generator.
OTP Bank was able to rally to a new high of 7,605 forints before surrendering to sell orders and finishing at 7,245 forints, down 255.

Brewery company Soproni Sorgyar Rt finished unchanged at 6,100 forints after the Deputy CEO of Brau Union Hungaria, which owns the recently merged Soproni and Martfui breweries, said higher profits were expected for the first half of 1997 compared to the same period of 1996.
BUX futures traded mixed with September maturity ending at 8,600 points, down just 0.5 points.
